_readme: Nordic and Baltic university directory. Every fact comes from the official national portal or ministry listed in each country's "sources". Update "checked" when you re-verify a country. Ownership is null when no official source states it.

countries.name: Sweden
countries.scope: Every university and university college that admits students through University Admissions in Sweden (40 institutions).
countries.ownershipNote: Public = state higher education institution; private = independent education provider, as classified by the Swedish Higher Education Authority (UKÄ).

rules.applicationFee: SEK 900 per semester for citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland. One fee covers all the programmes you choose in that round. Doctoral applicants pay no fee.
rules.tuition: Citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland pay tuition for bachelor’s and master’s studies. Each university sets its own amount — it is shown in the search results on University Admissions and on the university’s website. Doctoral studies are free of tuition fees.
rules.english: English 6: IELTS Academic 6.5 with no section below 5.5 · TOEFL iBT 4.5 on the new 1–6 scale (no section below 4) or 90 with writing 20 on the old scale · Cambridge C1 Advanced 180 · PTE Academic 62 (writing 61). Some degrees taught in English count instead of a test — see the official page.
entry: Bachelor’s: completed upper secondary (high school) education, English 6 and Mathematics 1a, 1b or 1c, plus any specific requirements of the programme.
Master’s: a bachelor’s degree equivalent to a Swedish kandidatexamen, English 6 and the programme’s specific requirements.

scholarships.label: Swedish Institute Scholarships for Global Professionals

rules.scholarshipNote: Many universities also offer tuition-fee scholarships to fee-paying students — see each university’s website.

countries.name: Finland
countries.scope: All 13 universities and 22 universities of applied sciences listed by Study in Finland.
countries.ownershipNote: All are publicly funded: universities are public-law corporations or foundations funded by the State, and universities of applied sciences are public limited companies in the Ministry of Education and Culture’s branch.

rules.applicationFee: €100 for applicants from outside the EU/EEA (Studyinfo application fee).
rules.tuition: Students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland usually pay tuition for English-taught bachelor’s and master’s programmes — typically €9,000 to €20,000 a year depending on the university and programme. Doctoral programmes are tuition-free. Universities often offer scholarships to fee-paying students.
rules.english: IELTS, TOEFL, PTE and Cambridge English are commonly accepted. Minimum scores are set by each university and programme.
entry: Bachelor’s: a school-leaving certificate that qualifies you for higher education in your home country. Some programmes add entrance exams, SAT or interviews.
Master’s: a bachelor’s degree. Master’s programmes at universities of applied sciences also require two years of relevant work experience.

deadlines.label: Joint application for autumn 2027 start opens
Joint application for autumn 2027 closes (15:00 Finnish time)

rules.deadlineNote: Some programmes run separate applications (mainly December–January) or rolling admission — check the programme on Studyinfo.fi.
rules.funds: Residence permit: at least €800 a month (€9,600 a year) — the minimum set by the Finnish Immigration Service.
rules.scholarshipNote: Scholarships for fee-paying students are offered by the universities themselves — see each university’s tuition-fee page.

countries.name: Norway
countries.scope: Every institution listed by Study in Norway (the Directorate for Higher Education and Skills): universities, specialised universities and university colleges.
countries.ownershipNote: Study in Norway and NOKUT group institutions by type, not by ownership, so we do not label them public or private here. Fees for non-EU students apply at public institutions too.

rules.applicationFee: Not specified by Study in Norway — check the institution’s admission page.
rules.tuition: Degree-seeking students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland must normally pay tuition fees. Amounts vary by institution and programme. Doctoral candidates and students on schemes such as NORPART, NORHED, Fulbright, Students at Risk and some Erasmus Mundus degrees are exempt.
rules.english: Document your English according to the institution’s requirements. Accepted tests and scores vary from institution to institution.
entry: Bachelor’s: the Higher Education Entrance Qualification — foreign qualifications are assessed against the official GSU list for your country. English-taught bachelor’s programmes admit through the institution’s own system.
Master’s: a recognised bachelor’s degree comparable to 180 ECTS, including at least 1½ years of full-time study in a relevant subject. Some programmes set a minimum grade average.
rules.deadlineNote: Each institution sets its own deadline for international applicants — see the institution’s admission page.
rules.funds: Residence permit: at least NOK 170,368 a year (NOK 15,488 a month) for 2026–2027, in addition to tuition.
rules.scholarshipNote: Some institutions, such as the University of Oslo, state that they offer no scholarships that cover tuition.

countries.name: Lithuania
countries.scope: Every university and college that lists English-taught programmes on Study in Lithuania (26 institutions).
countries.ownershipNote: Study in Lithuania does not say which institutions are state or private, so we only mark ownership where the institution’s official name says it is a state institution.

rules.applicationFee: Set by each university and programme.
rules.tuition: Study in Lithuania gives average fees of €2,000–€5,000 a year for bachelor’s and €3,000–€6,000 a year for master’s studies (FAQ last updated 2023). The exact fee is on each programme page.
rules.english: Set by each university and programme — see the programme’s “More information” page.
entry: Each university runs its own admission. Your documents go through recognition and subject-equivalence checks, which can take a month or longer — apply early.
rules.deadlineNote: Deadlines for the autumn semester at most universities are in June. Several universities also offer a spring intake.
rules.funds: Living costs: about €500–€800 a month depending on the city (Study in Lithuania).

countries.name: Latvia
countries.scope: Every institution featured on Study in Latvia (the State Education Development Agency), with the number of English-taught programmes it lists, plus the Latvian Academy of Music from the Ministry’s list.
countries.ownershipNote: Public = “State” and private = “Private”, as labelled by Study in Latvia.

portal.label: Apply directly to each university (often via DreamApply)

rules.applicationFee: A non-refundable application fee of around €150–€200.
rules.tuition: From under €1,600 a year for some bachelor’s programmes up to €25,600 for an Executive MBA. The fee for each programme is on Study in Latvia and the university’s website.
rules.english: English at CEFR level B2 or higher. How you prove it depends on the country where you studied.
entry: Bachelor’s: a secondary school certificate that allows you to enter the chosen studies.
Master’s: a bachelor’s degree in a relevant field. Your diploma is assessed by the Academic Information Centre (AIC).
rules.deadlineNote: Study in Latvia says non-EU applicants should apply by the beginning of June for the autumn semester and by mid-October or the beginning of November for spring. This guidance dates from 2021 — confirm the date with the university.
rules.funds: Living costs: about €450–€700 a month (Study in Latvia).
